title: Find Packet: Find packet details multiple matches in a frame
description:
When searching packet details with Find Packet, step through
each field that matches the search, using the currently selected
field as a starting point for searching the current frame before
going onto another frame.

Handle both forwards and backwards, so that backwards searching
initially finds the last match in each frame.

Part of #11269. (Packet bytes searching should presumably also
be handled.)

notes.body: Works well for me with Hex, String and RE in both directions, but for display filter doesn't highlight the bytes or find > 1 item in the same frame.

Yes, display filter doesn't work, it's handled by a different part of the code. It doesn't highlight the bytes for display filter either (that is, it doesn't happen currently without this MR), which is related to #17394 - I don't think in general we have a good way to get the fields that matched the filter.

We can get the list of field infos that were primed, so all those that were tested as part of the filter, but not which ones caused the match.

I added some GUI updates, would you mind taking a look at those?

I'm a bit undecided about two option for the top menu bar:

1. Leave existing actions, "Find Next" uses the current settings, finding multiple occurrences if that is checked and going to the next packet if not.
2. Add a "Find Next [Field|Occurrence]" actions (unfortunately, "CTRL-SHIFT-N" and "CTRL-ALT-N" are taken up by Find Next Mark and Find Next Time Reference) that look for the next occurrence within a packet, "Find Next" always goes to the next packet.
For item 2, could we use something like Alt-N and Alt-B?

I like it as this change stands.  I'd rather just use Ctrl-N and Ctrl-B subject to the checkbox than introduce more difficult-to-find key presses.

This preference (like the other find/search related options) are saved with the recent settings.  I think I am happy that its not part of what would be saved along with a profile, but I did type 'find' into Edit|Preferences|Advanced, then realised the strings begin with 'search', then realised it isn't part of prefs settings.

OK. I think I will leave it as it stands for now.

I think I'm ready to commit this, and then I'll follow up with another MR for multiple occurrences in packet bytes. (Part of the trick there is searching backwards.) Since the GUI item is disabled when searching for multiple occurrences doesn't work, I think this is OK as a standalone MR.

I don't like that the search frame is so big, do we need all this space?
I would like it to be more compact.

![Screenshot_2023-10-01_at_13.10.28](/uploads/a4a47bca80865f3fa8e9b7398b4b3ea9/Screenshot_2023-10-01_at_13.10.28.png)

Are you referring just to the vertical margin between the two rows (which looks bad, I agree, and much wider there on MacOS than on either Linux or Windows), or also to how the filter text edit doesn't need to get that large?

Possibly ideal would be something like Qt's [flow layout example](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwidgets-layouts-flowlayout-example.html) that would use a single line if there's enough space but break into two lines with less resolution, but I'm not sure how much work that would be.

I'm referring to both. When using a wide screen I would like one row, and using flow layout could be one way to support narrow screen.

The space between rows should be similar to other frames, like the filter expression frame (which also does not look good on a wide screen, it should be in one row).

OK, so part of it is doing whatever the filter expression frame does so that two rows don't look completely terrible on the default MacOS theme (maybe parts from your commit 61f73a3262fe724b7b31f14e842a80c5121301dd here). I don't have something to test MacOS with so I'm a little flying blind there. (I have Linux and Windows.)

The other issue is trying to make these accordion frame toolbars appear as one row on wide screen but two rows on narrow screen (so that narrow resolutions aren't literally impossible to use.)

I think that some of that is that the default MacOS theme has a fairly large default vertical spacing for QLayouts, and that explicitly setting the spacing property on the layout would help.

What happens if you start Wireshark with `-style fusion`?
Does !12381 look any better on MacOS?

Better, but I think it's not looking good on my screen.

commits_data.title: Find: Update search frame for Finding multiple fields
commits_data.message:
Find: Update search frame for Finding multiple fields

Add GUI support to turning on and off finding multiple occurrences
in a frame.

Also add a checkbox for searching backwards.

This makes the number of controls large, so split it into two rows.
